subject: Junior Backend Engineer: the reconciliation job I took from 41 minutes to 6
coverLetter:
Hello Lumen Ledger team,

Your ledger API turns payment events into a general ledger, and I've spent the last two years on the other side of that problem. At Tessellate Labs I built and still maintain the invoicing service that issues about 9,000 invoices a month, in Node.js, TypeScript and PostgreSQL.

The work I'm proudest of is boring on purpose. Our nightly reconciliation job took 41 minutes and had started overlapping the morning invoice run. I read the EXPLAIN output for a day, replaced row-by-row updates with set-based SQL, added two partial indexes, and got it to six minutes. At home I built ledger-lite, a small double-entry API where a Postgres constraint refuses any transaction whose debits and credits don't match. Someone on GitHub told me it caught a bug in their importer on day one.

You list AWS as a nice-to-have. I haven't used it in production; I moved four of our services to Docker Compose with health checks and wrote the runbook our on-call rotation uses, so containers and deploys aren't new to me, and I'm learning Kubernetes in the evenings.

If a junior engineer who likes the numbers to add up sounds useful, I'd be glad to talk.

Rania Haroon
whyUs: I've built invoicing and reconciliation code at Tessellate Labs, and ledger-lite, my side project, enforces balanced journal entries with a Postgres constraint. Lumen Ledger is working on the problem I keep choosing on my own time: making small businesses' books add up without someone staying late to find the missing rupees.
project: ledger-lite is a small double-entry bookkeeping API in TypeScript (Fastify and PostgreSQL). I moved the rule that every journal entry must balance out of the service layer and into a deferred constraint trigger, so no script can commit an unbalanced transaction. It has 140 stars on GitHub, and one user reported it caught a bug in their importer on the first day.
outreach: Hi, I'm Rania, a junior backend engineer in Lahore. I build invoicing and reconciliation services in Node.js, TypeScript and PostgreSQL at Tessellate Labs (I took our nightly reconciliation job from 41 minutes to 6). I just applied for the Junior Backend Engineer role and would value ten minutes to hear what the team is focused on this quarter.
